- **Pharma meets Ultra-Luxury? Be honest, how many Louis Vuitton handbags do you have? With the “consumer-grade pharma” mantra, I precariously keep one foot in the consumer brand world on purpose. Hospitality in particular. Not out of nostalgia, but because that’s where some of the most sophisticated commercial thinking lives out of necessity. In hospitality, you don’t just engage with customers…you live under the same roof as them. The stakes of experience delivery and the impact on brand can be immediate, personal, and unforgiving. Let's give this a shot…Meet the brand new Orient Express Corinthian, an LVMH brand experience. This breathtaking new vessel is more than a brand flex, its proof of what the brand-product-experience nexus can produce at its highest expression. I would argue that it can only exist because those dimensions are genuinely integrated. LVMH is of course known for luxury products: handbags, trunks, fragrances. What can be missed is that LVMH never confused the object alone for the proposition. The object was the entry point. The experience was always the story. Walk into a Louis Vuitton maison in Paris. Then one in Shanghai. Then Tokyo. Then São Paulo. The interaction follows the same choreography. A staff member in a different hemisphere, speaking a different language, raised in a different culture, delivers a recognizably identical experience. How? They’re operating inside a codified experience delivery system, not just following a set of guidelines or “winging it” from one interaction to the next. That system is what allows a brand rooted in physical goods to extend credibly to hotels, restaurants, and now to the "world’s largest sailing yacht". The offering evolves because the experience delivery system traveled. ❓ So here’s the question for pharma: what would it look like to use our new AI superpowers to build that kind of system in our industry context? Not a one-off training program. Not a set of brand-specific guidelines. A genuine experience delivery architecture that connects and orchestrates brand, product, digital and field engagement so seamlessly that a physician in Minneapolis and one in Madrid receive the same quality of interaction, regardless of what digital platform is being accessed or who’s standing in their office at the moment. ✅ I get it, pharma is not the same as the ultra-luxury segment. The connection can be architectural, not literal. So, maybe the opportunity for pharma isn’t to simply admire what LVMH built across product, brand and experience. It’s to ask what can we learn from that architecture that can be adapted to this industry in service of patients, HCPs and colleagues. I would love to hear thoughts from the industry... ...more**

- **What’s on your whiteboard this week? At the moment, mine is fully covered and a pretty messy with more lenses on shifting commercial "value narratives" in pharma... I'm doing this because, on my journey into that mythical world of pharma commercial organizations, I’ve learned that it is far better for "experience" to be viewed as an investment and value drive, rather than a cost center. At the core of this crusade is a simple but important realization: Many pharma commercial systems are super-optimized to generate prescribing intent through promotional activity, but often they are far less rigorous when it comes to what happens after the script is written…which is increasingly experiential territory. The whiteboard explores how this dynamic creates a “realization gap” where enormous amounts of patient and commercial value quietly leak away. Key points on the board: — Experience is not adjacent to the commercial model. It increasingly determines whether progression continues or stalls across the post script journey. —In the AI era, whether HCPs and patients interact with people, agents, workflows, apps, or portals, every interaction becomes brand defining and progression shaping. —Experience built upstream into the commercial system functions as an investment that protects realization. Experience retrofitted downstream after friction surfaces is often treated as a cost center. The takeaway for me? The future of pharma commercial will not be defined solely by who creates prescribing intent most effectively. It will increasingly be defined by who operationalizes experiential continuity most effectively between script and persistence. So, a question for you and your team: If post script value realization is increasingly governed by experiential continuity rather than promotional intensity, why is experience still treated as an adjacent support function rather than a core commercial discipline? ...more**

- **Trying to accelerate Ai? Have you tried turning to the underdog in your building? Rudy. Rocky. Muggsy Bogues. We all love a good underdog story. In the corporate arena, the contact center may be the ultimate underdog. Written off. Underestimated. Too often treated as a cost center. Yet it continues to punch above its weight in Ai out of sheer necessity. Working at the commercial intersection of pharma and consumer-grade experience has taught me how easily value is lost when trust, clarity and support break down. The consumer world has taught me something equally important: inside "outlier brands", direct customer service and support interactions are not devalued as back-office functions. They are an essential listening system, an intelligence system, and a source of operational and brand truth. That’s why, as Customer-Centric Marketers, we need to start viewing and valuing the contact center, our humble underdog, differently. Here's why: Despite being “targeted for termination” by the T-800 combat chassis (Google it!) of agentic Ai, the humble contact center may actually be the most advanced practitioner of applied, “real” Ai in your enterprise. While marketing races to become Ai-driven, the contact center has been quietly running old-school Ai for years. Natural language processing, machine learning, real-time behavioral intelligence, automated routing, sentiment detection, conversation analytics, etc. Now, it is also leading the way with many new-school Ai applications. This isn’t happening because the contact center wants to be trendy or visionary. It’s happening because the contact center doesn’t have a choice. When millions of real human interactions hit your system every day, you either build systems that can listen, interpret, route, respond, and learn at scale, or you fail and your brand equity gets crushed in front of the customer. Necessity, it turns out, is a far more effective innovation driver than any aspirational marketing Ai roadmap. So the takeaway for CMOs, marketing and commercial leaders is this: Accelerate your Ai adoption today…the nuanced customer intelligence you are spending significant capital trying to build may already exist inside your organization…it just may not be part of your coveted marcom stack. This month’s edition of The Customer-Centric Marketer (Edition #24) makes the case for why one of the most overlooked and undervalued functions in the enterprise may be the most trusted source of acceleration, lessons, signals, and truth for marketing in the age of Ai. Join 1700 Fellow Customer-Centric Marketers and Subscribe Today: https://lnkd.in/ejXZttvn #CustomerExperience #Marketing #AI #ContactCenter #CMO #CX #TheCustomerCentricMarketer ​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​​ ...more**

As I begin partnering with my very first client for the recently launched The Customer Excellence AGENCY , I am spending less time on solutions and more time framing challenges... With that, I focused on a simple question: What do we really know about our HCP customer? Beyond her specialty, prescribing data, and decile. I explored how she actually exists in and experiences the broader world…beyond our personas, channels and CRM systems. THE CONCLUSION? She’s a human being...and she lives in a world shaped by the simplicity, consistency, and seamlessness of the consumer brands that she relies on, trusts and loves in her “Other Life” outside of our purview… WHY IT MATTERS? That’s the standard she brings with her into her interactions with us, and the lens she uses to judge us. This is the gap…It’s not necessarily an Ai gap, data gap, pre-call planning gap, or targeting gap…It’s a context gap. THE WORK? This is one of pharma’s greatest untapped opportunities. Until we truly understand our HCP customers in her fulll context, we will continue designing experiences that make sense to us…but not to them.
